I will still farm the way I know, not chase too many new things at once. On my 5 mu, I will keep the heavier money for the crops that bring cash, so I will put more land and more fertilizer on chili, and keep cucumber, eggplant, and kidney bean a bit smaller. I only finished primary school, but after 50 years in the field I do watch carefully. I start from what worked last year, then I adjust a little by water, soil, and price. With well water in hand, I do not let the field go dry at flowering and fruit setting, because that is where yield is won or lost. Fertilizer costs money, but losing yield costs more, so I will not cut too hard. For chili and eggplant, I will feed more. Cucumber also eats a lot, especially potash, otherwise the fruit gets weak. Kidney bean I will hold lighter on nitrogen, because if I push too much, it runs in vine and pod set is poorer. I will use improved or hybrid seed where I saw neighbors get a steady harvest, but I will not change everything at once. On this small area, family labor is still the base, so I will keep tillage simple with rotary work on most plots and do spraying on time rather than after the problem spreads.
